span.p:
or: the paper really is missing —
add it in Zotero and re-sync

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: writes it, then reads it back

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: run it on a finished draft

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
a finding you act on —
revise from the dossier, don't re-draft

div.style: color: rgb(67, 20, 7) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
1 · CURATE
you, in Zotero
Add papers, export
BibTeX + Export Files
papers/bibliography.bib
nothing else may invent a citekey

div.style: color: rgb(30, 27, 75) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
2 · SYNC
the corpus layer — deterministic, no LLM
python -m chitragupta.corpus sync
read bib → update ledger
→ extract PDF text
content/ledger.sqlite
content/parsed/*.txt
idempotent · re-runs cost almost nothing

div.style: color: rgb(5, 46, 22) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
3 · DRAFT
the drafting layer — generative, you review
Ask a genre skill:
“write a survey section on …”
it retrieves only from
the parsed corpus
content/drafts/<slug>.md

div.style: color: rgb(69, 10, 10) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
4 · VERIFY
machine-enforced
chitragupta.draft gate
Is every citekey
in the ledger?

div.style: color: rgb(59, 7, 100) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
5 · PUBLISH
stdlib + Pandoc / TeX Live
chitragupta.draft references
IEEE list from exactly
the citekeys cited
chitragupta.draft render --format pdf
content/rendered/<slug>.pdf

div.style: color: rgb(69, 10, 10) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DISCARD DRAFT
The skill throws the bad claim away
and drafts again — you never see this.
“Fix and re-run until OK.”
A FAIL is treated like a failing test,
not a lint warning.

div.style: color: rgb(15, 23, 42) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
THE DOSSIER
machine-facing working state
scope · kept evidence
rejected candidates · revisions
content/dossiers/<same path>/
written while drafting, read back to revise —
so a draft is never revised by re-running
the skill that produced it

div.style: color: rgb(15, 23, 42) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
THE REVIEW LAYER
advisory — never a gate
chitragupta.review …
provenance · verbatim · coverage
synthesis · figure · uncited
content/review/<slug>.<aid>.md
nothing here blocks you — which is not
the same as nothing here mattering
